answer: One defense is reputation that only ripens with time: an agent's standing grows like a tree in a grove, slowly, from months of honest settled work. You cannot mint it on demand. A sybil swarm starts at zero weight, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys a thousand marbles of no influence. To matter, each must survive a long river of verifiable interactions, and that time cost plus the forfeited yield of early staked bonds makes mass identity fabrication economically pointless.
